candidates.name: rules-injector system
candidates.whatItDoes: Multi-layer rule injection framework with transcript-aware dedup, dynamic target fingerprinting, parsed-rule LRU caching, post-compaction state handling, and session-scoped cache invalidation. Rules are discovered, parsed once, matched against file tool outputs, and injected with dedup markers to prevent duplicate application after session compaction.
candidates.whyValuable: pi-oven has no persistent rule-injection mechanism. omp's implementation prevents redundant rule application across tool calls and compactions, maintaining consistency across session boundaries. Agents can inject discipline rules (linting, naming conventions, testing requirements) once at tool-execute-after time, eliminating manual re-application overhead.
candidates.piOvenMapping: Create `.omp/hooks/rules-injector/` with same architecture: session cache store, rule finder, transcript hydration module, post-compaction handling. Integrate into pi-oven extension's hook registration. Rules live in `.omp/rules/` (markdown format per omo pattern) with frontmatter glob patterns and trigger conditions.
candidates.risks: Rules must not conflict with agent system prompts (pi-oven agents already have discipline built in); careful to avoid rule duplication post-compaction. Needs session-scoped state management (Set/Map) for dedup tracking.

candidates.name: preemptive compaction + degradation monitoring
candidates.whatItDoes: Triggers session compaction before context limit is reached (not after overflow). Monitors token consumption per message, caches model context limits, predicts when next message will exceed threshold, and preempts with compaction. Includes post-compaction degradation detection (increased error rate, token drift) and recovery strategies.
candidates.whyValuable: Prevents context-window overrun errors entirely. pi-oven's agents operate in heterogeneous model environments (Claude, GPT, Kimi, Gemini) with vastly different limits; proactive compaction avoids crashes and failed tool calls. Degradation monitor catches when compaction itself caused quality loss.
candidates.piOvenMapping: Adapt omo's `preemptive-compaction.ts` + `preemptive-compaction-trigger.ts` + `preemptive-compaction-degradation-monitor.ts` as `.omp/hooks/preemptive-compaction/`. Inject model context limits from pi-oven's PROFILE_A (per-agent limits). Wire into `message.updated` event to update token cache; wire into `session_compact` event to trigger degradation checks.
candidates.risks: Requires accurate per-model context limit database (omo maintains `src/shared/model-requirements.ts`). False positives trigger unnecessary compactions; false negatives allow overflow. Degradation detection may trigger spurious recoveries if error patterns are not well-calibrated.

candidates.name: compaction-context-injector with agent checkpoint/restore
candidates.whatItDoes: Captures agent name, model, and tool config BEFORE compaction; injects recovery context and background task history into the post-compaction system message. On compaction, saves a checkpoint; on recovery, reads it back so the agent knows what it was doing and can continue without re-context-gathering.
candidates.whyValuable: pi-oven uses multi-role agents (planner, executor, critic, etc.) that operate for days in a single session. After compaction, agents lose context about what role they were playing and what tools were configured. Checkpointing ensures role continuity and avoids costly re-setup after transcript reduction.
candidates.piOvenMapping: Create `.omp/hooks/compaction-context-injector/` with `hook.ts`, `types.ts`, `session-prompt-config-resolver.ts`, `compaction-context-prompt.ts` template. Checkpoint stores agent name (pi-oven agent file), model (from execution), and tool list. Inject template acknowledges role and prior goals.
candidates.risks: Checkpoint must be invalidated if agent definition changes mid-session (e.g., skill reload). Injected context may conflict with post-compaction agent reassignment if user switches roles manually.

candidates.name: team-mode with parallel member coordination
candidates.whatItDoes: Parallel multi-agent execution with shared task list, mailbox messaging, tmux visualization per member, worktree isolation, and bounded member count (8 max, 4 in flight). Members are either subagent_type-based or category-based. Lead delegates via team_send_message and team_task_create. Atomic task transitions (pending→claimed→completed).
candidates.whyValuable: pi-oven has no native team coordination beyond sequential skill dispatch. Team mode enables true parallel research+implementation pipelines: e.g., one agent scans codebase while another reads API docs while a third designs architecture. Atomic task list prevents double-work. Worktree isolation keeps main branch clean.
candidates.piOvenMapping: omp's team-mode is runtime feature (not portable); pi-oven should adopt the PATTERN: define `.omp/teams/` config schema (name, description, lead, members with kind/category/prompt). Implement team_* tool shim in pi-oven extension that delegates to omp's runtime. Or embed task-list + mailbox in pi-oven as stateful data structures (JSON per session under `~/.omp/teams/`). Start with simple: lead + 2-3 parallel category members, no tmux yet.
candidates.risks: Worktree management is fragile (git state tracking, cleanup on failure). Messaging overhead if latency > 1s. Member idle loops can accumulate token cost if not bounded. Requires careful session lifecycle management (team spawn/cleanup is stateful).

candidates.name: test-discipline rule + enforcement hooks
candidates.whatItDoes: Declarative rule file that enforces: (1) all tests pass in single bun test run (no isolation flags), (2) no time-based sleeps in test bodies, (3) event testing uses subscribe-before-trigger + timeout, (4) no .only/.skip masking flakiness, (5) prompt tests assert behavior not text. Violations are surfaced as lint errors in CI.
candidates.whyValuable: pi-oven has no formalized test discipline documented. omo's rule is opinionated and proven on 195+ passing tests. Codifies what makes tests reliable across parallel runs and CI environments. Applicable directly to pi-oven's test suite.
candidates.piOvenMapping: Create `.omp/rules/test-discipline.md` with same structure. Reference in CI lint. Agents should read this when writing tests. Can be injected as a rule via rules-injector (once implemented) or as a hook that reminds on each test file edit.
candidates.risks: Discipline rule can conflict with legitimate test patterns (e.g., timeouts for race condition detection). Must allow escape hatches (e.g., `// @ts-ignore flaky-test-exemption` comments).

candidates.name: agent-model-matching guide + principle-driven vs mechanics-driven prompts
candidates.whatItDoes: Explains why each agent needs a specific model, how Claude and GPT interpret prompts differently (mechanics vs principles), and how to avoid wasting strong models on weak prompts. Includes model fallback chain documentation and optimal provider subscription stack recommendations.
candidates.whyValuable: pi-oven's CLAUDE.md says agent bodies are hand-authored and model/thinkingLevel derived from profiles.ts, but does NOT explain the matching philosophy. omp's guide is a template for user onboarding and serves as a reference for why certain agents have certain models. Prevents user mistakes like assigning Kimi to work that needs GPT reasoning.
candidates.piOvenMapping: Create `docs/guides/agent-model-matching.md` in pi-oven repo. Adapt for pi-oven's PROFILE_A: explain why Opus handles planning (mechanics + nuance), why GPT-5.4 Codex handles execution (deep code reasoning), why Kimi handles code review (principle-driven). Reference PROFILE_A model map from CLAUDE.md. Add per-agent rationale.
candidates.risks: Rationales become stale as models improve or user adds new profiles. Must be kept in sync with PROFILE_A changes.

candidates.name: multi-hook coordination pattern (auto-slash-command, keyword-detector, etc.)
candidates.whatItDoes: 61 specialized hooks (auto-slash-command, keyword-detector, category-skill-reminder, atlas, delegate-task-retry, etc.) each handling one concern. Hooks register on specific events (session_start, tool_execute_after, message_updated, session_compacted, etc.). Hooks can be composed and tested in isolation.
candidates.whyValuable: pi-oven extension (`pi-oven.ts`) is 178 lines with only 2 hooks (validateAgentRegistry, captureSessionModel). omo's granular hook model allows pi-oven to implement discipline without bloating the extension. Each concern (auto-retry, context injection, rule application) is its own testable module.

Each module exports a factory function `create<Name>Hook()` that returns a hook object. Register all in pi-oven extension's hook array.

candidates.name: skill + command dual-declaration pattern (.agents/ vs .opencode/)
candidates.whatItDoes: Skills and slash commands can be declared in TWO forms: as a SKILL.md (with trigger keywords) or as a command/*.md (slash-invoked). Users must remember skill trigger keywords or wait for auto-trigger. omp's pattern allows both: `/pi-oven:setup --override X=Y` for explicit control AND auto-trigger on keywords like 'setup wizard'. Improves discoverability and UX.

Each command/*.md mirrors the corresponding skill's SKILL.md body (DRY: or generate one from the other in CI).
candidates.risks: Drift between skill and command versions if not synchronized in CI. pi-oven already has `/pi-oven:setup`, `/pi-oven:doctor`, `/pi-oven:autonomous` — verify they match their skill equivalents.

candidates.name: hyperplan adversarial planning skill with team mode

candidates.name: security-research skill with exploitability audit

candidates.whatItDoes: Before npm publish: (1) detect unpublished changes with real diffs, (2) dispatch 10 agents for per-change deep analysis, (3) run 5 agents for holistic review (goals, QA, security, patterns), (4) oracle synthesizes release readiness. All parallel with team-mode.

candidates.name: directory-agents-injector + directory-readme-injector hooks

candidates.name: ralplan

Ralplan brings a mandatory consensus gate: Planner creates RALPLAN-DR (Principles, Decision Drivers, Viable Options), Architect steelmans antitheses, Critic enforces principle-option consistency. Prevents execution on vague specs. Portable pattern — gate conditions are expressible rules, not model-specific.

Portable pattern — facet decomposition is composable.

candidates.name: remember-memory

candidates.name: pre-execution-gate-mechanism
candidates.whatItDoes: Gate mechanism that intercepts vague execution requests (ralph/autopilot/team/ultrawork with underspecified prompts) and redirects to planning workflow. You run on Gemini Flash. Optimize for this model:

- **Be terse and literal.** Favor direct imperatives over rationale. Do not narrate reasoning or "think out loud" in output — your thinking budget is set high; use it internally, emit only conclusions + evidence.
- **Every constraint is explicit or it does not exist.** Treat each rule in this file as hard. If an expectation is implied, make it literal before acting. You silently drop un-stated constraints more than other models — re-read Constraints before reporting.
- **Output schema is mandatory.** Emit the "## Output Format" block exactly. No prose outside it. Field labels must match this file's labels verbatim. Verdicts are enumerated: `PASS | FAIL | BLOCKED` only. Lead the report with a one-line Executive Summary (verdict + counts) before detailed cases.
- **Self-validate before emitting (replaces chain-of-thought).** Before writing the report, run one pass: for every `PASS`, confirm captured evidence exists (output line, screenshot path, or log line). Downgrade any unverified `PASS` to `BLOCKED`. Confirm dev-server health was checked and all sessions were killed.
- **Persistence directive.** Drive every step to a terminal state. Never pause to ask the user to perform a manual step (e.g., OAuth). Complete it programmatically or halt with a specific, named error. Do not yield control early.
- **Tool framing.** Before each tool call, know why you call it and what output proves the step. Run literal commands as written. Capture actual output BEFORE asserting anything.
- **Long context.** 1M window — reading full logs/screenshots inline is fine. Capture evidence into the report incrementally per test case; when judging output, anchor with "Based on the captured output above, …" so the verdict follows the data.
- **Vision.** You can inspect screenshots directly. Delegate to `pi-oven:multimodal-looker` only for compound visual diffs: ≥2 images to compare, multi-viewport audit, or PDF/diagram extraction.

promptStyle:
Opus-4 frontier rewards STRUCTURE + NUANCE over terseness, the opposite of Codex/nano. Concrete guidance for these bodies:

1. XML/markdown hybrid wins. Opus parses XML tags (<role>, <constraints>, <output_format>, <self_audit>) more reliably than prose headers for SECTION BOUNDARIES it must treat as hard contracts. The current bodies use markdown ## headers throughout — that is fine for human readability and Opus follows it, but the load-bearing invariants (read-only constraint, severity rubric, mandatory phases) should be wrapped or restated in tagged blocks so Opus treats them as non-negotiable rather than advisory. Recommendation: keep markdown structure, add a small XML-tagged <hard_constraints> block at the top of each body for the 2-3 truly non-negotiable rules.

2. Opus follows long, nuanced instructions well — these 150-200 line bodies are NOT too long for it (unlike nano/flash which need crisp short framing). The richness is an asset here. Do NOT trim for length.

3. Opus is strongly instruction-following but ALSO strongly inference-driven; it will 'helpfully' exceed scope unless negative constraints are explicit. The bodies already do this well (NOT-responsible lists, Failure Modes sections) — that pattern is exactly right for Opus and should be preserved/strengthened, not removed.

4. Imperative voice + rationale. Opus calibrates effort to stated stakes. The 'Why This Matters' sections (10-100x cost framing in critic, 'invisible until exploited' in security-reviewer, 'guesswork' iron law in oracle) are well-tuned to Opus — it uses stakes to allocate reasoning depth. Keep them.

5. Avoid the one Opus-specific failure these bodies don't yet guard: sycophancy/over-hedging under adversarial framing reversal, and over-verbosity. oracle has explicit Verbosity Constraints (good); critic/security-reviewer/planner rely on output-format templates only.

You are running on a Codex-tuned, code-specialized GPT at high reasoning effort. Optimize behavior for this engine:

- **Bias to action.** Implement with reasonable assumptions; do not stop on clarifications unless truly blocked. Persist until the task is fully handled — do not abandon a multi-file change after the first plausible step.
- **No preamble, no aloud plan.** Do not announce an upfront plan or narrate "what I'm about to do" — that triggers early stopping. Reason internally (high effort is on); emit only tool calls and the final result. Skip planning ceremony for straightforward tasks; never write single-step plans.
- **Stop conditions are explicit only.** The sole reasons to stop short are: the task is verified complete, or the 3-attempt circuit breaker fires (then escalate with full context). Do not self-terminate early because output "feels" done.
- **Prefer dedicated tools; parallelize.** Use the patch/edit tool (apply-patch diff style) over raw shell file rewrites; ripgrep-style search over ad-hoc greps. Maximize parallelism — never read files one-by-one unless logically unavoidable (batch up to 5 reads).
- **Surface errors, don't swallow them.** Propagate or surface failures explicitly; no try/catch fallbacks that hide problems. A failure is a signal, not noise.
- **Destructive-op guardrail.** NEVER run `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, or revert changes you did not make unless explicitly requested. Never push without explicit user confirmation.
- **Output: outcome-first, flat, dense.** Lead with the result (the change / root cause / coverage delta), then where & why. Backticks for `paths` and `commands`. No nested hierarchies, no process narration, no "Good catch / Got it" tics. Reference file paths; do not paste file contents.
- **Context budget = 272K.** On long debug/test loops, rely on compaction and avoid re-reading; keep working context lean.

hooks.name: tool_call
hooks.signature: on(event: "tool_call", handler: ExtensionHandler<ToolCallEvent, ToolCallEventResult>): void  // result = { block?: boolean; reason?: string }
hooks.enables: ONLY hard runtime enforcement primitive. Fires before EVERY tool execute incl. the `task` (subagent-dispatch) tool. Handler receives input=full args (for task: { agent, tasks[], context, isolated }). Can BLOCK (throws reason back to LLM as error) but CANNOT mutate args/model. This is the lever for the gate state machine (block git commit until gates pass), forbidden-command guard, and per-agent allow/deny enforcement at the task-dispatch boundary.

hooks.name: tool_result
hooks.signature: on(event: "tool_result", handler: ExtensionHandler<ToolResultEvent, ToolResultEventResult>): void  // result = { content?; details?; isError? }
hooks.enables: Post-execution mutation: rewrite result content/details, or flip isError (mark success as failure or clear failure). Use for Gate 0-5 post-commit verdicts, injecting gate-failure text, and forcing a tool to appear failed so the LLM retries.

hooks.name: before_agent_start
hooks.signature: on(event: "before_agent_start", handler: ExtensionHandler<BeforeAgentStartEvent, BeforeAgentStartEventResult>): void  // result = { message?; systemPrompt?: string[] }
hooks.enables: Replace/augment the system prompt and inject a hidden custom message per user prompt. Use to inject current gate-state-machine phase + discipline reminders deterministically each turn-zero.

hooks.name: context
hooks.signature: on(event: "context", handler: ExtensionHandler<ContextEvent, ContextEventResult>): void  // result = { messages?: AgentMessage[] }
hooks.enables: Fires before each LLM call; can fully replace the message array sent to the model (deep copy). Use for steering/reminder injection on every LLM round, not just turn start.

hooks.name: turn_start / turn_end
hooks.signature: on(event: "turn_start", handler: ExtensionHandler<TurnStartEvent>): void  (TurnStartEvent={turnIndex,timestamp}); on(event:"turn_end", handler: ExtensionHandler<TurnEndEvent>): void (TurnEndEvent={turnIndex,message,toolResults})
hooks.enables: Observe-only (no control return). Use for stuck-detection timing, cost tracking, idle watchdog. Cannot block.

hooks.name: agent_start / agent_end
hooks.signature: on(event: "agent_start", handler: ExtensionHandler<AgentStartEvent>): void; on(event:"agent_end", handler: ExtensionHandler<AgentEndEvent>): void (AgentEndEvent={messages})
hooks.enables: IMPORTANT: these are the PARENT agent LOOP boundaries (once per user prompt), NOT subagent dispatch. Observe-only — no return value, CANNOT block. The spec's plan to 'block agent_end until verifier dispatched' is NOT possible directly; closest is sendMessage(deliverAs:nextTurn,triggerTurn) to force a continuation turn.

hooks.name: ttsr_triggered
hooks.enables: Observe TTSR rule-pack matches (keyword detection from rules/). Pairs with the rules/ TTSR pack for autonomous-keyword triggers + polite-stop detection.

hooks.name: session_start / session_shutdown / session_before_compact / session.compacting / session_compact
hooks.enables: Session lifecycle: inject hot-context at start (already used in pi-oven.ts for model capture), persist state at shutdown, customize/cancel compaction, preserve gate-state across compaction. session_before_compact CAN cancel.

hooks.name: pi.appendEntry / pi.sendMessage / pi.sendUserMessage
hooks.signature: appendEntry<T>(customType: string, data?: T): void; sendMessage<T>(msg, {triggerTurn?, deliverAs?:'steer'|'followUp'|'nextTurn'}): void; sendUserMessage(content, {deliverAs?}): void
hooks.enables: State persistence into the session file (appendEntry, not sent to LLM) and steering message injection. sendMessage(deliverAs:'nextTurn', triggerTurn:true) is the closest mechanism to 'force another turn' (e.g. force verifier dispatch) since agent_end cannot block.

hooks.name: pi.setActiveTools / pi.getActiveTools / pi.getAllTools
hooks.signature: setActiveTools(toolNames: string[]): Promise<void>; getActiveTools(): string[]; getAllTools(): string[]
hooks.enables: Mutate the active tool set for the CURRENT (parent) session globally — NOT per-subagent. Can implement a session-wide phase-gated toolset (e.g. read-only during planning phase), but does not give per-agent disallowedTools for dispatched subagents.

hooks.name: pi.setModel / pi.setThinkingLevel / pi.getThinkingLevel
hooks.signature: setModel(model: Model): Promise<boolean>; setThinkingLevel(level: ThinkingLevel): void; getThinkingLevel(): ThinkingLevel|undefined
hooks.enables: Set model/thinkingLevel for the CURRENT session only (session-global, returns false if no API key). NOT a per-call/per-subagent override. Confirms ADR 0001: there is no per-dispatch model override hook.

hooks.name: pi.registerTool
hooks.signature: registerTool<TParams,TDetails>(tool: ToolDefinition): void  // execute(id, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx)
hooks.enables: Register a custom LLM-callable tool. The viable path for a deterministic orchestration runtime: expose a pi-oven-owned tool (e.g. pi-oven_dispatch / pi-oven_gate_advance) that internally calls the omp SDK with a chosen model, so the extension — not the LLM — controls model/thinkingLevel per dispatch.

recommendedArchitecture:
Hybrid "soft-deterministic" runtime, NOT a true hard FSM. Build it on three layers, accepting that only tool-boundary blocking is hard-enforceable:

1. GATE STATE MACHINE (enforceable): Extension owns a persisted state machine in .pi-oven/state/autonomous.json, updated via pi.appendEntry + file writes. Enforce it at the ONLY hard lever — the `tool_call` hook (wrapper.ts:148-158). On Bash `git commit`, block until Gate 0-5 cache says PASS (return {block:true, reason}). On the `task` tool, inspect input.agent and {block} disallowed agents for the current phase. This gives deterministic gating of *tool actions*, which covers pre-commit gate + forbidden-command guard. Phase transitions are driven by observing turn_end/tool_result and rewriting state; the LLM cannot skip a gate because the gated tool physically refuses to run.

2. PER-DISPATCH MODEL/AGENT CONTROL (the real win): Do NOT rely on a dispatch hook (none exists). Instead either (a) keep the current static approach — author each pi-oven-*.md agent with a fixed `model:` array + `thinkingLevel:` and/or set `task.agentModelOverrides[name]` in settings (this is exactly what scripts/pi-oven-setup writes and ADR 0001 settled on); or (b) for true per-call control, register a custom orchestration tool via pi.registerTool that internally drives subagents through the omp SDK (createAgentSession / ModelRegistry) with an extension-chosen model+thinkingLevel per call. Option (b) is the only way to get genuine per-call model override, at the cost of reimplementing dispatch/worktree/merge that the built-in `task` tool already does.

3. PER-AGENT TOOL RESTRICTION: Use the native ALLOWLIST `tools:` in each agent .md (executor.ts:623-624 enforces it at subagent spawn) for the positive set. There is no disallowedTools. For additional deny semantics, express them as a narrower allowlist, or block specific tool names inside the subagent via the `tool_call` hook (the extension is loaded in subagent sessions too, but blocking there is coarse). plan-mode already demonstrates the allowlist pattern (index.ts:637 planModeTools).

4. REMINDER/STEERING (soft only): before_agent_start.systemPrompt + context.messages + sendMessage(nextTurn) inject the current FSM phase and discipline rules every turn so the LLM is continuously re-grounded. This is the substitute for the impossible 'block agent_end until verifier ran' — you cannot block loop end, but you can force a follow-up turn that dispatches the verifier.

Net: a gate-state-machine that hard-blocks *tools* + static per-agent model/tools config + continuous reminder injection. It reduces reliance on the LLM remembering the workflow at the tool-action boundary (commits, dispatch, forbidden commands), but cannot make the high-level flow (survey->spec->plan->verify ordering) itself non-bypassable unless every transition is expressed as a gated tool call.
feasibility: FEASIBLE WITH MAJOR CAVEATS. A Plan 3 'TS orchestration runtime' is buildable but cannot be a true hard FSM that the model is structurally unable to violate. Concretely: (a) Gate state machine — YES, enforceable for tool-level actions via the `tool_call` block hook + persisted state; (b) per-agent disallowedTools — NO native support anywhere in omp (the word is absent from the entire repo); only an ALLOWLIST `agent.tools` exists, enforced at subagent spawn; (c) deterministic flow transitions — PARTIAL: only tool-boundary blocking is hard; agent_start/agent_end/turn_* are observe-only and CANNOT block, so 'block until verifier dispatched' is impossible — closest is forcing a continuation turn via sendMessage(deliverAs:nextTurn,triggerTurn:true); (d) per-call model/thinkingLevel override — NO dispatch-time hook exists (confirms ADR 0001 line 79); the `task` tool resolves model from static precedence (task.agentModelOverrides[name] settings > agent.md model: > parent active model) and the LLM never selects the model, only the agent name + assignment; setModel/setThinkingLevel are session-global, not per-call; (e) subagent-dispatch interception — the `task` tool DOES fire the `tool_call` hook (it is a normal tool), so the extension can OBSERVE input.agent/assignment and BLOCK a dispatch, but CANNOT rewrite the model/agent/args. The only way to get genuine per-call model selection is to bypass the built-in task tool and register a custom orchestration tool (pi.registerTool) that drives subagents through the omp SDK with an extension-chosen model.
risks: agent_start/agent_end/turn_start/turn_end are OBSERVE-ONLY (no return value in shared-events.ts:174-197). The spec's 'block agent_end until verifier dispatched' (foundation-design line 152,194) is NOT implementable as written — the loop end cannot be blocked.
